title: A Stonean hypercover of a prescribed profinite base
statement: Let $P$ be a profinite space (compact, Hausdorff and totally disconnected). There exists a simplicial object $S$ in the category of profinite spaces over $P$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Every $S_n$ is extremally disconnected and every augmentation $S_n\to P$ is surjective. For every $n\geq 0$, there is a limiting cone $M_n$ for the proper-face diagram [def-sfb-proper-face-diagram] and a surjective arrow $\mu_n:S_n\to M_n$ whose composites with every face projection are the corresponding simplicial operators. The vertex $M_0$ is exactly the identity object over $P$. Empty $P$ is allowed. Matching limits and all spaces are in the same universe as $P$.

proof.text: Work in the chosen universe with the category of profinite spaces over $P$, with finite jointly surjective families as coverings. Its fibre products $E\times_G F$ are the closed subspaces of $E\times F$ on which the two maps to $G$ agree; the terminal object is $P$. Take as basis the objects whose underlying spaces are extremally disconnected. For each $E\to P$, the Stonean-cover theorem gives a continuous surjection $\beta|E|\to E$, hence a singleton basis cover over $P$. Adjoining another basis arrow preserves joint surjectivity, including when the target is empty. Apply the finite-basis hypercover theorem to the terminal object. Obtain an augmented simplicial finite formal family $K_n=\{E_{n,i}\to P\}_{i\in I_n}$, with every $E_{n,i}$ extremally disconnected, and componentwise jointly surjective matching arrows. All the theorem's assumptions have been checked: fibre products exist, basis covers are finite, and adjoining preserves coverings.

source.place: Tag 0DAV, lemma-hypercovering-object; finite split-skeleton construction, with Bhatt–Scholze Example 2.4.6 for the basis

proof.text: Reindex each finite family by a finite set in the universe of P and transport all operators through the chosen bijections. Set $S_n=\coprod_{i\in I_n}E_{n,i}$, the finite topological disjoint union, and use the component maps for every simplicial operator. Finite disjoint unions of compact Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces have these same properties. The closure of an open set is the union of its closures in the finitely many clopen summands; it is open because each summand is extremally disconnected. Thus $S_n$ is Stonean. The formulas for composition in formal families show that these operators obey every simplicial identity and commute with augmentation. Realization preserves finite limits of finite formal families: an element of a limiting cone chooses one member at each vertex, with those choices compatible along every arrow, and then a point in the limit of the selected spaces. There are finitely many choices. Each choice cuts out a clopen piece of the ordinary finite limit, and its topology is the topology of that selected limit. This is precisely the family-limit construction, so its finite disjoint union is homeomorphic to the ordinary limit. The empty diagram gives the one-member terminal family over $P$. Consequently the realized formal matching objects are the proper-face matching spaces of $S_\bullet/P$. Over each selected matching member, the original covering family is jointly surjective; hence each realized matching map is surjective.

source.place: Tags 01G2 and 0DAV: finite limits of formal families and the matching-cover condition, realized by finite disjoint unions

proof.text: The degree-zero matching arrow gives a surjection $S_0\to P$. For $n>0$, choose any order-preserving surjection $[n]\to[0]$. Its simplicial operator gives a map $S_0\to S_n$ over $P$. For each $p\in P$, a point of $S_0$ above $p$ therefore gives a point of $S_n$ above $p$. Every augmentation $t_n:S_n\to P$ is surjective. If $P$ is empty, every profinite space over $P$ is empty and all assertions are vacuous.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_common_stonean_hypercover (P : Profinite.{u}) :
    ∃ S : SimplicialObject (Over P),
      ∃ (M : ∀ n : ℕ, Cone (S.properFaceDiagram n))
        (μ : ∀ n : ℕ, S _⦋n⦌ ⟶ (M n).pt),
        (M 0).pt = Over.mk (𝟙 P) ∧
        (∀ n : ℕ, Nonempty (IsLimit (M n))) ∧
        (∀ (n : ℕ) (b : SimplicialObject.ProperFaceCategory n),
          μ n ≫ (M n).π.app (op b) = S.map b.obj.hom.op) ∧
        (∀ n : ℕ, Function.Surjective (μ n).left) ∧
        (∀ n : ℕ, ExtremallyDisconnected (S _⦋n⦌).left) ∧
        (∀ n : ℕ, Function.Surjective (S _⦋n⦌).hom)
